findings.title: Shutdown ordering test can miss the race it targets
findings.suggested_fix: Synchronize on evidence that the Shutdown goroutine has started attempting shutdown before releasing the blocked Commit, using an explicit test hook or a deterministic lock/handshake arrangement instead of treating a 100 ms timeout as evidence of contention.
findings.first_evidence: The test accepts the 100 ms timeout and releases the blocked Stringer without establishing that Shutdown ran or attempted to acquire admitMu.
findings.why_it_matters: If the Shutdown goroutine is delayed until after release, even an implementation that inserts the quit marker before the admitted request can pass: Commit resumes, queues its request, and the commit loop can process it before Shutdown runs. The test therefore does not reliably detect the ordering regression it is intended to catch.
evidence: lib/batcher/batcher_test.go:292-296: after starting Shutdown, the test waits for b.closed or 100 ms, ignores the timeout branch, and then closes blocker.release.

lib/batcher/batcher_test.go:24-34: blockingStringer holds Commit inside the debug log until release is closed, so the test has a controlled admission pause but no handshake showing Shutdown has reached the admission lock.

testing_gaps: The race-ordering regression test uses a bounded delay rather than deterministic synchronization to establish Shutdown contention.
